reasonsTitle: Why are babies so captivated by crinkle sounds?
reasonsLead: What sounds like mere noise is, for a baby, packed with comfort and brain-building discovery.

reasons.title: Like sounds from the womb
reasons.body: The blood-flow and placental sounds a baby heard in the womb are very close to high-frequency, crinkly noise. Instinctively it recalls that safe place and brings calm.

reasons.title: Discovering cause and effect
reasons.body: Around 6–12 months, babies begin to grasp cause and effect: "I moved it, so it made a sound!" Getting a 100% response to their own action is the best kind of entertainment.

reasons.title: Multi-sensory
reasons.body: It stimulates hearing (a clear, high sound), touch (crinkly, smooth textures), and sight (sparkly, shifting shapes) all at once — a strong presence even for babies whose eyesight is still developing.

reasons.title: Imitating grown-ups
reasons.body: Around 18 months to 2 years, babies enjoy it as imitation of adults. Seeing a parent rustle a shopping bag sparks the curiosity to do it too.

ageLead: As babies grow, the sounds that resonate change too. Here is a guide to choosing toys that match each stage from 0 to 2 years.

ageGuide.intro: With eyesight still developing, babies respond strongly to sound. Crinkly, rustling sounds like a shopping bag resemble womb sounds, so they often calm a crying baby or spark interest.

toys.name: Cloth books & crinkle cloth toys
toys.desc: Cloth toys that rustle like a plastic bag when touched. Dedicated toys avoid choking risk and can be fully washed for hygiene.

toys.name: Rattles & bead balls
toys.desc: Toys that jingle and shake when moved. A mesh, easy-to-grip ball rattle is a classic first toy.

toys.name: Pull-out style toys
toys.desc: Knowing toys that mimic pulling tissues or tearing newspaper — the tearing and crinkle sounds in one.

ageGuide.theme: Sounds that change with their actions
ageGuide.intro: Rather than crinkle sounds alone, babies now delight in toys that respond to their own action — hitting, pressing — with sound.

toys.name: Sound books & instrument toys
toys.desc: Books that play songs or animal sounds at the press of a button, and drums or xylophones to strike.

toys.name: Ball drops & spiral slopes
toys.desc: A dropped ball rolls down, rattling and chiming. They learn cause and effect and repeat it endlessly.

toys.name: Pull toys
toys.desc: Pull the string and an animal or car clatters along behind. Great for walking practice.

ageGuide.theme: Building a sense of achievement and sociality
ageGuide.intro: With more dexterous hands, imagination, cognition, and sociality develop fast. They graduate from sound-only toys toward ones with a sense of "I did it!"

toys.name: Play-kitchen sets
toys.desc: Pretend play recreating everyday sounds — the "chop" of cutting hook-and-loop veggies, pots clattering.

toys.name: Shape-sorters & blocks
toys.desc: The click of a piece fitting, and the crash of a tall stack tumbling down.

toys.name: Talking picture dictionaries
toys.desc: Touch an illustration with a pen and hear its name or sound — perfect for the vocabulary-explosion age.

ageNote: ※ Product examples are common favorites and are not endorsements or advertisements.
safety: Real plastic bags can block the mouth or nose and cause suffocation, or be torn and swallowed. Never let a baby play with one directly.
For real play, use safe baby toys such as commercial crinkle cloth books or washable "plastic-feel" toys.
This app makes sound. Have an adult set the volume and avoid long continuous use.
When playing on a phone or tablet, an adult must always be present.
tipsLead: A few ways to get the most out of it with your baby.

tips.title: Sit together
tips.desc: Hold your baby on your lap so they feel safe, and tap along with them.

tips.title: Keep it gentle
tips.desc: Start at a low volume. Babies prefer soft, clear sounds over loud ones.

tips.title: Add words
tips.desc: Narrate what happens — "sparkle!", "pop!" — to grow early language.

tips.title: Short and sweet
tips.desc: A few minutes at a time is plenty. Use the timer to wind down.

tips.title: Wind-down routine
tips.desc: Womb-sound and sleep mode help settle before naps and bedtime.

tips.title: Follow their lead
tips.desc: Let your baby set the pace — repetition is how they learn and feel joy.
